comparable_cases.why_comparable: Same address (1701 Fillmore St), same zoning (NCT-Fillmore), same use (self-service/fast food restaurant continuation). This is the most recent Planning approval for the subject property itself.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved continuation of the existing self-service/fast food restaurant use at this address in 2016 via agency referral. The space is already established as a restaurant, so Super Duper Burgers would be a restaurant-to-restaurant tenant change without a change of use requiring Planning Commission review.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Directly across the street at 1700 Fillmore St, NCT-Fillmore zoning, restaurant use. ABC Type 47 referral approved in 2022 for non-formula retail restaurant.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral explicitly notes the restaurant is 'non-formula retail use' and was approved. This suggests Planning tracks formula retail status even in routine referrals and may apply different scrutiny; the parenthetical suggests formula retail restaurants might require additional process.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Roam Artisan Burgers at 1923 Fillmore St (252m away), another burger restaurant in the Upper Fillmore NCD, ABC Type 41 approved in 2022. Very similar concept to Super Duper Burgers.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: ABC referral for Roam Artisan Burgers, a fast-casual burger chain, was approved without mention of formula retail status. Roam has multiple Bay Area locations but was treated as non-formula retail, suggesting not all multi-location burger concepts trigger Sec. 303.1.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: I'a Poke at 1515 Fillmore St (218m south on same corridor), NCT-Fillmore zoning, fast-casual restaurant, ABC Type 41 approved April 2023, most recent comparable on Fillmore St.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Recent agency referral approved for a fast-casual restaurant on Fillmore St without formula retail issues mentioned. Demonstrates routine approval for restaurant continuations in NCT-Fillmore when formula retail controls do not apply.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Restaurant at 1560 Fillmore St (170m away), NCT-Fillmore zoning, DPH referral approved June 2021. Same district and use type.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Another agency referral for restaurant continuation in NCT-Fillmore approved routinely in 2021. Reinforces pattern that restaurant-to-restaurant changes in this district are processed as referrals without discretionary review when no formula retail or other special controls apply.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Restaurant at 1740 O'Farrell St (218m away), NCT-Fillmore zoning, DPH referral for existing restaurant use approved August 2020.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral explicitly states 'existing restaurant use within the Fillmore Street Commercial Transit District per Planning Code Section 760' was approved. Confirms restaurant use is principally permitted in NCT-Fillmore without discretionary review.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Restaurant at 1581 Webster St (148m away), Japantown NCD adjacent to subject, ABC Type 41 approved April 2023 for full-service restaurant.

Decision notes restaurant use is permitted per PC Section 721 and must operate as Bona Fide Eating Place per Section 202.2(a)(1). Shows consistency of restaurant approvals in adjacent districts.

timeline_cost.notes: If a Conditional Use Authorization is required, the timeline is 120–300 days from CUA filing to approval: pre-application meeting, environmental review, Section 311 neighborhood notification (300-foot radius, 30-day comment period), Planning Commission hearing, and 30-day appeal period. CUA fees in NCT-FILLMORE for formula retail were approximately $3,150 in 2023 (CPI-adjusted from $2,747) and rise with construction cost; expect $3,100–$6,000 depending on tenant improvement value, per comparable CUA records. If no CUA is required and the project proceeds as a restaurant continuation via agency referral, the timeline is 14–60 days for health plan check and 14–120 days for the building permit, depending on plan complexity and whether a change of occupancy is triggered; government fees would be approximately $2,000–$4,000 (business registration, health plan check $828–$2,207, health permit $470, building permit $800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation, sign permit $300–$1,500). The ranges above assume a CUA is required and include only the CUA application fee and building/health fees; they do not include state registration, insurance, or tenant improvement construction costs. These are times to approval when granted; if the CUA is denied, no timeline to approval applies.
timeline_cost.path: Conditional Use Authorization (Planning Code § 303); Health permit to operate

status_definitions.allowed: Allowed: the cited records or code sections show this approval is available as of right, or already exists for this space, without a discretionary hearing.
status_definitions.further_review: Further review: the approval is obtainable only through a discretionary or multi-step review (a hearing, a referral, a licence investigation) whose result the records do not settle.
status_definitions.potential_blocker: Potential blocker: a cited rule, cap or record could stop this approval or force a change to the concept unless a specific condition is met.
status_definitions.not_permitted: Not permitted: a cited code section prohibits this use or approval at this address as the concept is described.
status_definitions.insufficient_information: Insufficient information: the records in hand do not show whether this approval is needed or obtainable; the could-not-establish section says what would settle it.

confidence_definitions.verified: Verified: stated directly by a cited record or code section that applies to this exact address, parcel or zoning district.
confidence_definitions.likely_applicable: Likely applicable: inferred from cited records of comparable cases or from a general rule; not stated for this address.
confidence_definitions.needs_confirmation: Needs confirmation: plausible but not supported by a record in hand; confirm with the agency or document named.
confidence_definitions.professional_review_required: Professional review required: depends on plans, an inspection, or legal or design judgment that public records cannot supply.

records_summary: 1701 Fillmore St is zoned NCT-FILLMORE (Fillmore Street Neighborhood Commercial Transit), where restaurant use is principally permitted. The site currently operates as a self-service/fast food restaurant (approved 2016-11-15 for continuation). The address sits within two Special Use Districts—Family and Senior Housing Opportunity SUD and within 1/4 mile of an Existing Fringe Financial Service—neither of which restricts restaurant uses. The immediate area is highly active: 14 food/drink businesses within 500 ft, including 4 bars, and 11 active on-sale ABC licenses within the same radius (53 within 1,000 ft). Within 1,000 ft over the last 10 years, only 7 dated use decisions are on file: 5 approved, 1 approved with conditions, and 1 denied; too few for a meaningful approval rate.
data_gaps: Formula retail threshold analysis: the records do not show whether a 2,950 sq ft restaurant in NCT-FILLMORE triggers Planning Code §303.1 formula retail controls when the use does not change.

The pathway rules state new use permission is 'not decided' because the existing use is restaurant and the description does not say whether that business stays; no definitive zoning answer is provided for a continuation versus a new tenant.
No extracted hearing transcripts or decision rationales for the two noteworthy CUAs (Pinot's Palette, Orangetheory) or the denied entertainment CUA.

ABC concentration metrics: the records flag undue concentration but do not show the census tract ratio or whether 1701 Fillmore falls in a high-crime or over-concentrated tract (not applicable here, as no alcohol is proposed).
No details on conditions attached to the 2023 AMC Theaters CUA approval beyond the four listed.
